en: edited by Mahāmahopādhyāya Hara Prasād Śāstrī.
1. In *Advayavajrasaṃgraha*, GOS 1927, Baroda, edited by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai; 2.
In the *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō*.
The reality accepted by the Sugata is free from both eternalism and nihilism.
Regarding phenomena that are by nature unborn, the speech of a beast consists of affirmation and negation. (1)
To one who says "it exists," we reply: from the perspective of investigation, everything does not exist.
To one who says "it does not exist," we reply: from the perspective of non-investigation, everything exists. (2)
In whatever manner superimpositions arise for the practitioner of reality, in that very same manner those superimpositions are destroyed by the practitioner of reality. (3)
Since the innate (*sahaja*) is uncontrived, attachment is not innate;
there is no bliss other than the innate, and bliss has the characteristic of non-attachment. (4)
Having realized the Self as free from attachment and having attained the true bliss of dwelling within it,
and having made the entire universe his own abode, he is immersed in the ocean of the innate nature (sahaja).
The yogi established in the reality of mantra is grounded in the state of non-attachment;
having made you his guru, he shall become one whose sphere is non-attachment.
This work is by the venerable Paṇḍita-Avadhūta Śrīmad Advayavajra.
